ceiling.

Break the test file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.

2. All imports still resolve; all existing tests pass without modification to
   their assertions (move-only refactor).

  assertions or test logic.

# Canonical full suite excludes `packages/` tests (tui 30 + shared 13 files)

*Discovered from WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (canonical suite root-level `tests/` coverage).* That item closed the `tests/` gap by replacing the two narrow `suiteCommands` with the umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`. It deliberately kept its scope to `tests/`, so the `packages/` gap remains.

**Note:** file counts have grown since the work item was created — `packages/tui` now has 30 test files (was 22) and `packages/shared` has 13 (was 12). The `packages/herdr` count is 129, unchanged. Repository total: 453 test files (up from 440).

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (the single source of full-suite evidence for `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate and audit F3) resolves only to `tests/`. Tracked test files by location:

| Location | Test files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` | 277 | Yes (since WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR) |
| `packages/herdr` | 129 | No — producer decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); opt-in `--type herdr` / `--group herdr` |
| `packages/tui` | 30 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| `packages/shared` | 13 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| **Repository total** | **453** | **277** |

`packages/tui/**/*.test.ts` (30 files, all under `packages/tui/extensions/`) and `packages/shared/**/*.test.ts` (13 files) run under a bare `npx vitest` / CI but are referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths, so no gate can execute or cache-evidence them. (Note: a `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`.)

## Goal

Every `packages/` test file is either executed by the canonical full suite (or a cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths), or has an explicit documented exclusion with a rationale — the same standard WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR applied to `tests/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.pi/test-config.json` covers `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` tests (in `suiteCommands`, or as named `groups` entries wired to their paths so `implement.py finish` selects them), or each exclusion is documented with a rationale in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`.
- A full `/skill:test` run (`python3 <test-skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --json`) reports the newly covered files as executed, with the executed-file count recorded in the work item.
- Any failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the "Test gates" section is shared, not duplicated) carries the updated coverage table (files executed / excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Evidence-path constraint:** full-suite evidence for the audit resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new `groups.*` entry alone does not satisfy a "full suite passes" AC (see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → "Cache evidence scope").
- **Vitest filters are substring matches** on the repository-relative path, so `packages/shared` / `packages/tui` can be selected by positional filters (`-- tests` umbrella does not cover them; `-- packages` would also pull in `packages/herdr`, which is excluded by producer decision).
- **Do not re-litigate the herdr decision** (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix; `groups.herdr` added by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN).
- Measure runtime before/after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`), not ad-hoc `npx vitest`.
- Beware the `run_tests.py --suite node` trap: that suite name resolves through the legacy convention path (`tests/{unit,node,cli}`) and ignores `suiteCommands`; use the default `--suite all` for canonical runs.

## Existing state

The canonical suite is a single command: `npm --silent test -- tests` (277 files, ~791 s vitest duration, ~1065 s wall clock). The `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`. There is no group for `packages/shared`.

## Desired change

Add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to the canonical full suite coverage. The simplest approach is to add additional commands to `suiteCommands`:

```jsonc
{
  "suiteCommands": [
    "npm --silent test -- tests",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/shared",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/tui/extensions"
  ]
}
```

This adds two positional filters that are precise: `packages/shared` matches only the 13 shared test files, and `packages/tui/extensions` matches only the 30 tui test files (all under `extensions/`), neither of which would match `packages/herdr`.

Alternatively, create named groups (`shared`, `tui`) and wire them into `suiteCommands` as separate commands — same effect, but with changed-scope selection benefits.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to `suiteCommands` (or create named groups + wire them)
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — update the coverage table and runtime section
- `vitest.config.ts` — no change expected; existing config handles `packages/` correctly

## Related work

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** — closed the `tests/` coverage gap (umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`); records the OPEN QUESTION that became this item.
- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — herdr package suite excluded by producer decision (won't-fix).
- **WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN** — added `groups.herdr` to `.pi/test-config.json`.
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** — source of the additional-gap evidence for `packages/tui/extensions/**`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should packages/herdr be included?" — Answer (work item description): No — producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix. Source: work item description.
- Q: "What about the `tui-extensions` group that already exists?" — Answer: It is not wired into `suiteCommands`, so it provides no full-suite gate coverage. The brief proposes wiring it (or creating an equivalent group) into suiteCommands. Source: inspection of `.pi/test-config.json`.
- Q: "File counts have changed since the work item was created — should we update the title?" — Answer: Yes — the title should be updated to reflect current counts (30 + 13, not 22 + 12). Source: `git ls-files` on current tree.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Runtime increase (medium).** Adding 43 files to the canonical suite increases wall-clock. *Mitigation:* measure before/after with `run_tests.py`; `timeoutPerCommand` is 3600 s, so there is headroom.
- **New coverage may surface pre-existing failures (medium).** Neither `packages/tui` nor `packages/shared` has run under the canonical gate, so latent failures could appear. *Mitigation:* triage into `test-failure` items (AC3).
- **Filter precision (low).** `packages/shared` and `packages/tui/extensions` are substring filters; verified against `git ls-files` that they match only the intended 13 + 30 files and not `packages/herdr`. *Assumption:* `packages/tui` has no test files outside `extensions/` (confirmed: 30/30 are under `extensions/`).
- **Scope creep (low).** `packages/herdr` is explicitly out of scope (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); covering it would require re-litigating a closed won't-fix decision. Any further gap (e.g. a new package) becomes a linked work item, not added scope.
- **Assumption:** adding commands to `suiteCommands` (rather than only `groups`) is required, because `--type full` evidence resolves from `suiteCommands` only (evidence-path constraint). A group-only change would not satisfy AC2.

# Make groupings stable

## Problem statement

When the herdr selection list re-sorts on refresh, items sometimes move from
one group to another even though nothing about them changed materially. This
causes disconcerting movement in the list. The list should only change when
the underlying items change in a material way (e.g. a new key file is added,
or the priority changes). Additionally, items should sort in priority order —
all high items ahead of medium, all medium ahead of low.

## Users

- **Herdr users / producers** who watch the worklist to decide what to work
  on next. A stable list lets them track where work sits; gratuitous movement
  breaks their mental model of the queue.
- **Producers reviewing the in-review queue** who rely on a predictable
  within-group order to find the most important work first.

User story: *As a Herdr user, I want the worklist grouping and ordering to be
a stable function of the items themselves, so that an item only changes
group when its content (key files, priority, stage/status) or the item set
changes — and within each group, high-priority items always rank above
medium, which rank above low.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Group assignment is **content-deterministic**: for a fixed set of items
      with fixed key files / priority / stage / status, the group each item
      lands in is identical regardless of the order in which the items are
      presented to the grouping algorithm (canonical ordering applied before
      the greedy first-fit packing). A transient change such as an
      `updatedAt` timestamp (comment added, audit run) must never change an
      item's group.
- [ ] An item's group membership changes **only** when a material input
      changes: its key files section, its priority, its stage/status, or the
      item set itself (item added/removed). Verified by a stability test
      that perturbs non-material inputs (`updatedAt`, input order) and
      asserts group labels/numbers are unchanged.
- [ ] Within each group (Critical Group N and Group N), items sort by
      **priority first (high → medium → low)**, then by the existing stage
      sub-order (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then by
      id — so all high items appear ahead of all medium items, which appear
      ahead of all low items. The `in_review` 6-bucket comparator already
      sorts priority-first and keeps that behaviour.
- [ ] The change is applied **and kept in sync** in both mirrors: core
      `wl next` / `wl worklist` grouping (`src/commands/grouping.ts`,
      `src/worklist-selection.ts`) and the herdr plugin copy
      (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`); shared grouping tests cover both
      copies.
- [ ] `wl next -n N` and the herdr worklist still emit the canonical section
      order (Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review) with no
      regression in existing grouping/smart-selection behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
      comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Greedy first-fit file-path conflict detection is retained — the change
  makes it order-independent, it does not replace the packing strategy.
- Herdr plugin has zero npm dependencies and cannot import from
  `src/commands/`; the mirror must stay a self-contained pure duplication
  (per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B decision Q2c).
- The always-show-mandatory guarantee of `selectWorkItems`
  (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) is preserved — grouping only
  reorders and stamps, never filters or drops items.
- Default `maxGroups` of 3 for file-path-based groups is unchanged.

## Existing state

- `regroupWorkItems` (herdr) / `selectBrowseFeed` (core) recompute group
  assignments on every refresh from the merged selection.
- `groupItemsByFilePaths` is a greedy first-fit over items **in input
  order**; the input order fluctuates with `updatedAt` (comment/audit
  churn), so the same item set can pack into different groups across
  refreshes. That is the root cause of the observed group hopping.
- Within-group ordering (`compareGroupableItems`) currently sorts by stage
  sub-order first (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then
  priority; `in_review` items already sort priority-first.

## Desired change

1. Make `groupItemsByFilePaths` (and hence `assignItemGroups`) a pure
   function of the item content: sort/canonicalise the input items by a
   stable content-derived key before greedy packing, so group membership
   depends only on ids, key files, priority and stage/status — not on
   transient ordering.
2. Make priority the **primary** within-group sort key in
   `compareGroupableItems` (both mirrors), keeping the stage sub-order as
   the secondary key.
3. Keep the two mirrors in sync and extend the grouping tests in both
   locations with stability assertions (order perturbation + non-material
   input perturbation must not change group membership or ordering).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — core `groupItemsByFilePaths` / `assignItemGroups` / `compareGroupableItems`; canonicalise input order; priority-first within-group sort.
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — core `selectBrowseFeed` grouping pipeline consuming `assignItemGroups`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — mirrored plugin copy of the same algorithm; must stay in sync.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems`; input order source feeding `regroupWorkItems` (contract only — no functional change expected unless needed for canonicalisation).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — callers of `regroupWorkItems`.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — core grouping tests; add stability assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — plugin grouping tests; mirror stability assertions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Within-group order change is intentional but observable:** making priority
  the primary within-group sort key changes which item of a group renders
  first (stage sub-order becomes secondary). Existing tests in
  `grouping.test.ts` / `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` that assert the old
  stage-first order must be updated deliberately, not incidentally.
- **Canonicalisation key must be content-derived:** the pre-pack sort key
  (e.g. priority + stage + id) must never include timestamps or insertion
  order, or the instability simply moves to the new key.
- **Assumption — "material change" definition:** key files (the `**Key Files:**`
  section), priority, stage/status, or item-set membership. Description prose
  outside the Key Files section already cannot affect grouping
  (`extractFilePaths` reads only that section) and stays non-material.
- **Scope-creep guard:** out-of-scope opportunities (stable group *labels*
  across renumbering, configurable `maxGroups`) are recorded as related/future
  work, not implemented here.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite `assignItemGroups` + `next.ts` ordering (completed; produced the current grouping spec this item stabilises).
- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order) (completed; established section order + `regroupWorkItems`).
- WL-0MUY1CSQG007TCYX — actively-worked items derived from `status === 'in-progress'` (affects group membership inputs).
- WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G — in_review priority-first ordering (precedent for priority-first within-group sort).

### Related work (automated report)

Low-relevance automatic matches (find-related): WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C (Bubble
up critical items), WL-0MRSGMTYY0062WFJ (audit-set fail hard), WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9
(needs-producer-review filter) — adjacent selection-list behaviour, no AC
overlap with this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should priority ordering apply? (A) within each group only, (B) globally across the whole list, (C) both" — Answer (producer): **A — within each group only**. Source: interactive reply (intake round, recommended option accepted).
- Q2: "Stability definition — (A) content-deterministic grouping via canonical sort before fit, (B) keep packing, only stabilise within-group ordering" — Answer (producer): **A — content-deterministic grouping**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted).
- Q3: "Scope of the change — (A) both mirrors kept in sync, (B) herdr only, (C) core only" — Answer (producer): **A — both, kept in sync**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted). Research: confirmed the duplicate lives at `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B Q2c.

# Manually created tabs go to the left, dispatched tabs to the right

## Problem statement

Tabs spawned by the operator from the Herdr Worklog selection list (e.g. `p` for plan, `i` for implement, `p-n` for a new pi session, or any other ID-carrying interactive dispatch) currently append at the **right** end of the workspace tab row, away from the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab they belong next to. Automated dispatch tabs (downtime dispatcher) append there too. Operator-created tabs should instead land immediately to the **left** of the Worklog/extensions tab, while automated dispatches keep today's right-side placement.

## Users

- The operator (producer/developer) driving work out of the Herdr Worklog selection list. Example user stories:
  - "As an operator, when I hit `i` to implement a work item, I want the new item tab to appear next to the Worklog tab so my manually opened sessions stay grouped and my work-in-progress tabs don't get pushed out of view at the far right of the tab row."
  - "As an operator, when I open a new pi session from the selection list, I want it beside the other manually opened sessions rather than at the end of a long tab row."

## Acceptance Criteria

- An interactive dispatch that **creates a new tab** (ID-carrying commands such as `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, prompt/`!!`/`!` commands carrying a work-item ID, and a new-pi-session dispatch from the selection list) places that tab immediately to the **left of the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab** in the invoking workspace.
- Automated dispatches (downtime dispatcher) place their tabs at the default right-side position exactly as today — no behaviour change.
- Tab repositioning is implemented via the herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` set to the extensions tab's index (or an equivalent herdr CLI/socket mechanism available at implement time); the tab is first created as today and then moved.
- Fail-open: when the Worklog/extensions tab cannot be resolved (no plugin pane, no tab labelled `Worklog`, multiple/ambiguous matches) or `tab.move` fails, the newly created tab stays at its default right-side position — the dispatch is never blocked, dropped, or placed in a wrong workspace.
- Reuse semantics are preserved: an **existing** item-ID tab is adopted without being moved (only freshly provisioned tabs are repositioned; a reused tab's position is the operator's own arrangement).
- At least one automated test (unit or integration) covers each of: left placement for an interactively created tab, default right placement for a dispatcher-created tab, and fail-open when the extensions tab or the move is unavailable.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No herdr core changes in scope: herdr 0.9.5 CLI `tab create` has no insert/position flag — the repositioning must go through the socket API (`tab.move` with `insert_index`) or an existing CLI mechanism, and must tolerate the capability being absent (fail-open).
- The "extensions tab" is the tab hosting the Worklog selection list / plugin TUI — i.e. the tab containing a pane labelled `Work Items` (`PLUGIN_PANE_LABEL`), commonly renamed to `Worklog` by `open-worklog-tab.sh`.
- Interactive and dispatcher callers share the same tab-creation choke points (`createTabInWorkspace`, the anchor resolvers); the change must distinguish the two so only operator-initiated creation repositions.
- Root-pane cleanup semantics (fail-safe liveness check, WS-holder placeholder close) and the fail-open dispatch guarantees from the interactive item-tab work must be preserved.
- Keep changes surgical; do not introduce a second tab mechanism or restructure the dispatcher-adoption logic.

## Existing state

- `herdr tab create` appends a new tab at the right end of the workspace tab row; both the interactive item-ID path and the downtime dispatcher path create tabs this way, so all tabs land to the right of existing tabs.
- Interactive ID-carrying dispatches provision a tab labelled exactly `<itemId>` via `getItemTabAnchor` (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`) — created on first use, adopted thereafter — split via `send-to-pi.sh`/`run-in-pane.sh` with `--anchor`, with fail-safe placeholder root-pane cleanup.
- The downtime dispatcher provisions its own tabs (Dispatcher workspace / project workspace item tabs) through the same herdr CLI tab primitives.
- herdr socket API exposes `tab.move` (with `insert_index`) and emits `tab.moved` events carrying the requested `insert_index` and the updated ordered tab list.

## Desired change

- At the tab-creation choke point, add an interactive-placement mode (e.g. a `placement: 'left-of-extensions'` flag/param, defaulting to today's behaviour) set only by the interactive dispatch path.
- After a freshly provisioned tab is created for an interactive dispatch, resolve the Worklog/extensions tab in that workspace (pane labelled `Work Items`, falling back to a tab labelled `Worklog`) and `tab.move` the new tab to `insert_index` = that tab's index (immediately left of it). Fail-open at every boundary.
- Dispatcher-created tabs, and adopted (reused) interactive tabs, are untouched.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — `createTabInWorkspace` (and any new `tab move` CLI/socket helper) — the tab-creation choke point.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor` provisioning path (interactive item-ID tabs).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` / `closeInteractiveTabRootPane` (interactive vs dispatcher call-site split).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` / `downtime-worker.pane.ts` — dispatcher tab provisioning (must remain right-placed).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — `PLUGIN_PANE_LABEL` (`Work Items`) and any new placement-mode types/labels.
- Tests alongside each module (`*.test.ts`) plus the split-guard baselines if CLI helper signatures change.

## Related work

- WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — "Implement: interactive item-tab placement" (completed) — established the interactive item-ID tab anchor + `--anchor` forwarding this work extends.
- WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS — "Pi processes should start in a work item tab" (completed epic) — parent of the interactive placement work.
- WL-0MUYI3K8H007MPKF / WL-0MUYI3JRC006115V — interactive item-tab root-pane cleanup (implement/test).
- WL-0MUYI3KPB0024U86 — "Docs: interactive item-ID-tab placement" (completed) — docs companion to update.
- WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG — "Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace…" (completed) — dispatcher anchor-by-ID workspace; the automated path that stays right-placed.
- WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane" (completed) — root-pane cleanup precedent.
- WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ (refactor) — decomposed `dispatcher-anchor.ts`; placement code now lives in the split modules above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Extensions-tab resolution ambiguity** — if multiple tabs contain a `Work Items`-labelled pane, or both a `Worklog`-labelled tab and a `Work Items` pane tab exist, the anchor choice must be deterministic; fail-open (leave tab right) on none/ambiguous rather than misplace.
- **herdr `tab.move` availability** — depends on the socket API of the running herdr (0.9.5 supports it); if absent or failing, the tab stays where created (right) — never block the dispatch.
- **Created-vs-reused signal** — repositioning must apply only to freshly provisioned tabs; reusing the existing `onCreate` create-vs-reuse observer avoids disturbing tabs the operator arranged manually.
- **Scope-creep risk** — reordering existing/adopted tabs, changing dispatcher (right) placement, or reworking the pane-splitting (non-tab) interactive paths are out of scope; record any such follow-up as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption: keybinding coverage** — `p`/`i`/`p-n` and other interactive dispatches resolve to the interactive `onCommand` path (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`); treat any interactive dispatch that creates a tab as operator-created. Non-tab (current-pane split) routes are unaffected.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What is 'the extensions tab'?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "(a) The tab hosting the Worklog selection list / plugin TUI (currently renamed 'Worklog')." Source: interactive reply, this intake session (WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW).
- Q2: "Acceptable implementation mechanism (herdr 0.9.5 CLI `tab create` has no insert flag)?" — Answer (operator): "(a) create the tab as today, then reposition via herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` = index of the extensions tab." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Which interactions count as operator-created, and where should the change live?" — Answer (operator): "(a) All interactive dispatch paths — item-ID tabs from `p`/`i`/other ID-carrying commands AND `p-n` new-pi-session tabs — moved left, applied in `packages/herdr` tab-creation code (`createTabInWorkspace`/anchor resolvers)." Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKVZ3RBL10DFPPW** – Use Alt+Right Arrow to advance focus (replace Tab) (completed)
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC** – Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUAT5D00443GA** – Impl: tab-focus-gated visibility in visibility.ts + docs (completed)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: automated, created, dispatcher, downtime, extensions, herdr, implement, left, list, manually, need, new, now, operator, place, plan, processes, right, selection, session, spawning, tab, tabs, they, when

# Refactor guard: init split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ — decompose `src/commands/init.ts` god class
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Position in chain:** 1 of 7 — blocks every extraction child.

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `src/commands/init.ts` split, I want one automated
gate that fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so
that every extraction child can land safely, no existing test assertion changes,
and no reviewer has to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4 require: no file over 1,000 lines, an unchanged public
surface at `./init.js`, unmodified test assertions, and an acyclic import graph.
Nothing in the repo enforces this for `src/commands/init*.ts` today. This child
builds the enforcement first, mirroring `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G) and `tests/interview/split-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MVXY34A900816MN).

Facts captured at plan time (2026-11-03, `dev`):

- `src/commands/init.ts` — 1,515 lines; public surface is exactly
  **2 exports**: default `register(ctx: PluginContext)` and named
  `isSorraAgentsInstalled(): boolean`.
- Consumers of `./init.js`: `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import, default)
  and `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` (default import). No external consumer imports
  `isSorraAgentsInstalled`, but it must stay importable (parent AC2).
- Three brittle **source-text** tests in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` read
  `src/commands/init.ts` with `fs.readFileSync` and assert hook-content strings
  (`tmp-worktree`, `git-common-dir`, `git-dir`, `const postCheckoutContent`,
  two `const centralScriptContent` occurrences). Those tests will break when
  child 4 moves the hook generators to `init.hooks.ts`.
- `tests/cli/init.test.ts` (584 lines) and `tests/cli/initialization-check.test.ts`
  (201 lines) are black-box CLI tests; they do not import init internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** guard `tests/cli/init/split-guard.test.ts` passes on the
   current tree before any production code moves.
2. Committed baseline `tests/cli/init/init.split-baseline.json` records the two
   public exports (value/default flagged separately) plus provenance (generation
   command, source commit, timestamp).
3. Public exports from the original module path remain importable unchanged
   (barrel re-export where consumers exist): default `register` and named
   `isSorraAgentsInstalled` are still importable from `src/commands/init.js`.
4. No file (original or extracted module) exceeds 1,000 lines — the size gate
   enforces the ceiling for every `src/commands/init*.ts` production module,
   driven by an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains only
   `'init.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever shrinks.
5. No new circular imports; module responsibilities documented — no production
   `src/commands/init*.ts` module contains a runtime import of `./init.js`, and
   the static import graph of `init*.ts` modules is acyclic.
6. Hook-content gate: the concatenated `src/commands/init*.ts` family source
   still contains `tmp-worktree`, `git-common-dir`, `git-dir`,
   `const postCheckoutContent`, and two `const centralScriptContent` blocks —
   so the hook generators remain behaviour-preserving wherever they live.
7. All existing tests pass without modification to their import paths or
   assertions (move-only, behaviour-preserving) — the three source-text tests
   in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` are generalised to read the whole
   `src/commands/init*.ts` family (concatenated) instead of only `init.ts`.
   **Assertion logic is unchanged** — only the source location is generalised
   so the tests pass before and after child 4. This is the only existing-test
   edit in the epic (see OPEN QUESTION below).
8. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a removed
   hook-content string) — failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite.
10. A comment records the baseline generation command and the gate-to-parent-AC
    mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `tests/cli/init/split-guard-scan.ts`: list `src/commands/init*.ts`,
   concatenate their source, parse the public exports, load the baseline.
2. Add `tests/cli/init/split-guard.test.ts` with four separately named `it()`
   checks (public surface, size+allowlist, cycle/barrel, hook content) and
   negative-case fixtures.
3. Generate `tests/cli/init/init.split-baseline.json` (provenance: command,
   `git rev-parse HEAD`, ISO timestamp).
4. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the test helper so the finalise child empties
   it in one line.
5. Replace the three `new URL('../src/commands/init.ts', ...)` reads in
   `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` with the family-concatenation helper; keep
   every `expect(...)` assertion byte-identical.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the output in a comment.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/cli/init/split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `tests/cli/init/split-guard-scan.ts` — new
- `tests/cli/init/init.split-baseline.json` — new
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — source-location generalisation only (3 tests)
- `src/commands/init.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- OPEN QUESTION (recorded on the parent): parent AC3 says "without modification
  to their import paths or assertions". This child changes neither an import
  path nor an assertion — it generalises the file read from `init.ts` to the
  `init*.ts` family. Producer to confirm this reading, or choose the fallback
  (keep hook content constants in `init.ts` and extract only the install
  functions).

# Audit runner: Phase-2 timeout + malformed-verdict persistence rejection on WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R

## Goal

Make the audit pipeline produce and persist a valid verdict for **WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R** ("Downtime dispatcher: the elected leader has no coordination entry …") so the item stops consuming release-gate remediation budget and can be classified correctly.

## Observed behaviour (2026-11-04, ContextHub, commit ce353516)

1. **Phase-2 timeout.** Two consecutive `audit_runner.py issue WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R --force --timeout 1800` runs reported:
   `"script_name": "pi (Phase 2 deep analysis)", "reason": "Phase 2 deep analysis timed out after 1800s"`.
   The second attempt was made inside the release gate's bounded remediation and exhausted the gate budget (`1865s of 1800s`), which blocked the release with a "budget exhausted — audit needs refreshing offline" reason.
2. **Verdict persistence rejection.** Even after a Phase-2 timeout, the persisted audit text for the item is:
   > "# Audit persistence notice … The audit pipeline completed, but the final persistence step rejected the assembled verdict content (malformed JSON / validation error). The full report could not be stored in the audit text field."
   So the stored `auditResult` is `readyToClose: false` derived from a **persistence failure**, not from an AC assessment. That makes a transient failure indistinguishable from a genuine "not ready to close" verdict to downstream consumers.

## Why it matters

- The release audit gate cannot tell a transient persistence failure from a genuine failing verdict, so it either blocks spuriously or burns its whole remediation budget on one item.
- An item that was never genuinely assessed is left with `readyToClose: false` persisted, which will keep blocking releases until a human re-audits.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the pipeline fails to assemble or persist a valid verdict, the persisted audit is marked **transient** (a distinguishable state such as a `transient`/`provider_error` classification, never a bare `readyToClose: false`), and the gate classifies it as transient — not as a genuine verdict.
2. Phase-2 deep analysis completes for `WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R` within the configured budget (or the item's Phase-2 is right-sized so it does not need a 1800 s call), and a valid, parseable verdict is persisted.
3. Tests cover: (a) a verdict-assembly/persistence failure is persisted as transient rather than `readyToClose: false`; (b) the release audit gate treats such an item as transient/remediable, not as a genuine blocker.
4. The full canonical suite passes (`/skill:test --scope full`).

## Blocking relationship

Blocks the current `dev` → `main` release (transient audit; gate budget exhausted on it).

---

## Plan (2026-11-05)

Pre-check: `decision=plan` (effort M, risk Medium). Plan-approval gate:
`request_approval=false` (the item is not Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe
risk), so no approval pause was required. Six automated review stages were run
and the AC coverage review was applied.

### Repository boundary (recorded assumption)

The affected code lives in the **SorraAgents framework repository**, not this
ContextHub checkout: `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`.
This item is ContextHub-owned (it was filed here by the ContextHub release
gate), so the children below are tracked in this store and are implemented in a
SorraAgents worktree (`skill/audit`, `skill/ship`, `tests/`); `wl` resolves the
`WL-` prefix to this sibling store. On completion the implementing session
records a SorraAgents record item — precedent: `WL-0MU0FHSEP003PCDY` →
`SA-0MVCP83RX005V1OW`.

### Duplicate / related-work check

`wl search` for "verdict persistence transient", "audit gate transient",
"Phase 2 timeout audit" and "malformed JSON verdict" found no ContextHub
duplicate (no overlapping completed item). Partial overlap exists with
SorraAgents framework items; this item covers only the remaining gaps and does
not re-implement their scope:

- `SA-0MW0LR0D70034DGE` (plan_complete) — parent for failure-notice persistence
  (header-first) and Phase-2 provider-error recovery. Its children
  `SA-0MW0LRBJM008Q2MC` (fix) and `SA-0MW0LR5GC007WIU9` (test) make the real
  report persist; they do **not** classify a residual persistence failure as
  transient, which is this item's gap.
- `SA-0MW0LSIGC008X8GS` (blocked traceability node) — "verdict persisted and
  readable" plus a malformed-content test. Partial overlap only: C1 asserts the
  transient *classification*, not report readability.
- `SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` (open, idea) — Phase-2 timeout diagnostic hardcodes
  `CALL_PI_TIMEOUT`. C4 absorbs that scope (truthful effective-timeout
  diagnostic) instead of duplicating it; the absorbing child cross-references
  it with a comment.

### Measured evidence for the Phase-2 budget

`python3 scripts/measure_audit_performance.py --root ~/.audit_debug --json`
(2026-11-05 corpus: 934 logs, 2,456 timing lines, read-only):

| context | calls | p50 | p90 | max | calls at 1800 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `phase2_deep` | 476 | 288 s | 1,085 s | 3,600 s | 15 |
| `phase2_child` | 454 | 341 s | 1,116 s | 2,071 s | 10 |
| `verdict_reask` | 211 | 462 s | 1,339 s | 2,372 s | 6 |
| `parent` (screen) | 719 | 215 s | 958 s | 3,153 s | 16 |

The Phase-2 family's p90 is ~1,085–1,116 s and 25 Phase-2 calls landed exactly
on the 1,800 s ceiling. Applying the repository's existing derivation
discipline (`ceil(p95 x safety factor 2)`, rounded) yields a ~2,400 s Phase-2
budget; 1,800 s is under-sized for the Phase-2 family, not merely a saturation
artefact.

### Decomposition

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|
| C1 | Test: transient classification of verdict failures | task | — |
| C2 | Persist transient classification and gate recognition | bug | C1 |
| C3 | Test: Phase-2 budget and gate remediation alignment | task | — |
| C4 | Right-size Phase-2 budget and gate remediation | bug | C3 |
| C5 | Verify forced re-audit and full suite | task | C2, C4 |

Test-first: C1/C3 are authored and confirmed red before C2/C4 make them green.
Each test/implementation pair is finished from the implementation child's
worktree at a green tip; a red suite is never pushed.

### AC coverage

- AC1 → C1, C2
- AC2 → C3, C4, C5
- AC3(a) → C1, C2
- AC3(b) → C1, C2
- AC4 → C5

### Assumptions / decisions

- **D1 — classification is content-scoped, not a new `wl` schema field.** The
  persisted audit keeps its `Ready to close: <Yes|No>` first line (the `wl`
  audit-text contract) and adds a machine-readable
  `Audit classification: transient (<cause>)` line to the report, mirrored into
  the `wl audit-set --summary`, which the gate recognises. Rationale: the gate
  already classifies from content (`isTimeoutOrTransientAudit`), and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` § "Design note: why Option B+ (not a
  durable marker)" rejected a ContextHub schema + CLI migration for a
  comparable flag. **No ContextHub schema/CLI change** is needed.
- **D2 — Phase-2 budget.** Raise the Phase-2 ceiling from 1,800 s to 2,400 s
  (measured p90 x 2), keep the Phase-1 screen budgets (1,080 s) and the 600 s
  stall abort unchanged, and clamp the ship gate's per-item remediation timeout
  to the remaining total budget so one attempt cannot overshoot it (the
  `1865s of 1800s` incident).
- **D3 — truthful timeout diagnostic.** The Phase-2 timeout message reports the
  resolved effective timeout rather than the hardcoded 1,800 s (absorbs
  `SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1`).
- **D4 — live verification is safe.** `WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R` is
  `completed`/`done`, so a forced re-audit cannot demote it through
  `wl audit-set`'s `in_review` reversion path; a "No" verdict is still a valid
  parseable verdict for AC2.

### Prototype / risk

No prototype is needed: the classification, budget and gate behaviours are
unit-testable with injectable runners. Residual risk: raising the Phase-2
ceiling lengthens a pathological run; it stays bounded by the 600 s stall abort
and the gate's total remediation budget clamp.

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were required — the ACs are testable and the design
choices were resolved from existing evidence. Decisions recorded for audit:

- Q: Should the transient classification be a new `wl` field? — Answer (agent,
  evidence-based): No; a content-scoped classification line. Source:
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` "Option B+" design note.
- Q: Is 1,800 s under-sized for Phase-2? — Answer (agent, measured): Yes; p90
  is ~1,085–1,116 s, 25 calls capped at 1,800 s. Source:
  `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py --root ~/.audit_debug`.
- Q: Which repository implements this? — Answer (agent, precedent):
  SorraAgents framework repo, ContextHub-owned worklog item. Source:
  `WL-0MU0FHSEP003PCDY` / `SA-0MVCP83RX005V1OW`.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-05: initial decomposition — 5 children (two test-first pairs plus a
  verification task), 4 dependency edges, duplicate check and measured Phase-2
  corpus recorded.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`
- `skill/ship/scripts/audit-remediation.js`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
- `tests/test_audit_runner_persist.py`
- `tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-audit-remediation.mjs`
- `tests/test_audit_transient_classification_docs.py`

> The affected code and tests live in the **SorraAgents** framework repository
> (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`); the audit's
> Phase-2 deep analysis may read these paths from the SorraAgents checkout or
> via the symlinked skill tree to verify the criteria.

# Persist transient classification and gate recognition

**Covers parent AC1 and AC3(a)/(b)** of `WL-0MW2F2T1I001ZNH7`. Depends on C1
(`WL-0MW32Y8E90092TIM`, tests first).

> **Repository:** SorraAgents framework repository (`skill/audit`, `skill/ship`,
> `tests/`, `docs/dev`). This work item stays owned by the ContextHub worklog;
> `wl` resolves the `WL-` prefix to the sibling store.
>
> **Do not duplicate:** header-first failure-notice persistence and Phase-2
> provider-error recovery are tracked separately in `SA-0MW0LR0D70034DGE`
> (`SA-0MW0LRBJM008Q2MC`, `SA-0MW0LR5GC007WIU9`, `SA-0MW0LROWQ000JVTM`). This
> change only adds the transient classification and the gate's recognition of
> it; it does not re-implement their scope.

## Goal

When the pipeline fails to assemble or persist a valid verdict, the persisted
audit is marked transient — a distinguishable state, never a bare
`readyToClose: false` implying a model verdict — and the release audit gate
classifies it as transient rather than as a genuine verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persist_audit._build_fallback_text` emits a `Ready to close:` first line followed by `Audit classification: transient (verdict_persistence_failure)`; the `wl audit-set --summary` written on that path names the transient classification.
2. Report assembly emits `Audit classification: transient (verdict_assembly_failure: <cause>)` (cause = `timeout` | `provider_error` | `unparseable_output` | `concurrency_cap`) whenever the run's AC verdicts came from an infrastructure fallback; a clean run emits no classification line.
3. `check-audit-gate.js` recognises the classification token as transient (not a genuine verdict) in both `rawOutput` and `summary`, and its transient patterns reach parity with the runner's `_INFRA_FALLBACK_MARKERS` (`Pi model output could not be parsed`, `Audit concurrency limit reached`).
4. A transient-classified item is reported as transient/remediable with a re-audit reason and is never reported with the genuine-verdict reason `Audit verdict: not ready to close`.
5. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the classification contract (line format, causes, gate behaviour) and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` documents the gate's recognition; a docs assertion test pins the wording.
6. No ContextHub schema or CLI change is introduced: no new `wl audit-set` flag; the classification is content in the existing `rawOutput` / `summary` fields.
7. The changed-scope suite, including the C1 tests, is green.

8. Parent AC coverage: when the pipeline fails to assemble or persist a valid verdict, the persisted audit is marked transient with a distinguishable classification (never a bare `readyToClose: false`), and the gate classifies it as transient rather than as a genuine verdict.

## Minimal implementation

- `persist_audit._build_fallback_text`: add the classification line after the verdict line; extend the summary passed to `wl audit-set`.
- `audit_runner._assemble_issue_report`: accept an optional classification argument and emit the line after `Ready to close:`; `_phase_report` resolves the cause from `ctx.ac_fallback_used` / `_evidence_has_infra_failure_markers` and passes it.
- `check-audit-gate.js`: add the classification-token pattern(s) to `isTimeoutOrTransientAudit`; keep the prose markers as a backstop; carry the transient classification into the report entry so a remediation that leaves it transient names the transient reason.
- Docs: add the classification contract to the two reference docs and a pinning test.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Deliverables

- Persisted transient classification with gate recognition, docs, and green C1 regression tests.

# Right-size Phase-2 budget and gate remediation

**Covers parent AC2 and AC3(a)** of `WL-0MW2F2T1I001ZNH7`. Depends on C3
(`WL-0MW32YGSY008GRQP`, tests first).

> **Repository:** SorraAgents framework repository (`skill/audit`, `skill/ship`,
> `docs/dev`). This work item stays owned by the ContextHub worklog; `wl`
> resolves the `WL-` prefix to the sibling store.
>
> **Absorbs:** `SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` (Phase-2 diagnostic hardcodes
> `CALL_PI_TIMEOUT`). Add a cross-reference comment on that item when this
> change lands so the scope is not worked twice.

## Goal

Phase-2 deep analysis has a budget sized from measured data (not the 1,800 s
placeholder), reports the timeout it actually applied, and cannot consume the

# Redirect post-push verification full-suite runs to a pinned isolated worktree

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run executed from the main checkout during post-push verification
can race with a sibling `implement.py finish` fast-forwarding the main
checkout's local `dev` (`git merge --ff-only`), swapping source files mid-run
and producing phantom failures (WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 evidence: 4 failures in
`tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` / `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` at
1abe9618; identical tree green in an isolated worktree minutes earlier).

## Goal (User Story)

As an AI agent running `implement.py finish`, I want post-push verification and
audit cache-miss full-suite runs to execute in an isolated worktree pinned to
the pushed commit — never live in the main checkout — so a sibling finish
fast-forwarding `dev` cannot swap the files a suite is reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mitigate the race:** the post-push verification path is updated so that
   full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned commit,
   and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout — not run live in
   the main checkout where a sibling finish can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
2. The post-push verification path (and the audit skill F3 cache-miss
   auto-execution path) resolves an isolated worktree for the commit being
   verified and executes the full suite there — not in the live main checkout
   where a sibling `finish` can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
3. The fresh cache entry produced by the isolated-worktree run is grafted into
   the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` before/mirroring the pre-push hook's
   `mirror_suite_cache` semantics (never overwrites an existing entry), so
   read-only post-push verification and audits serve the grafted entry.
4. The mitigation is minimal and localised: document + redirect test execution
   to worktrees; it does not rewrite the post-push verification pipeline or
   change verdict semantics (`green`/`red`/`missing`/`not_applicable`).
5. The single-owner main-checkout flock lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84) and the
   main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O) remain intact; finish refuses
   loudly rather than masking a real failure.
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish()` read-only
  verification step and Step-6 main-checkout dev fast-forward
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_tests_via_test_skill` /
  F3 auto-execution (`run_cached(..., cwd=per_audit_root)`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py` — suite execution
  and cache
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guidance to match

## Constraints

- Must not break the dev-push pre-push hook's cache mirroring
  (`mirror_suite_cache`, `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` in ContextHub /
  `.githooks/pre-push`).
- The audit skill's F3 cache-miss path must be covered (audits running in the
  main checkout face the same race).
- Worktree creation cost is assumed negligible (node_modules is symlinked);
  latency must stay bounded.
- Implementation repo: framework skills live in the SorraAgents repo
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`); run
  `wl` worktree-safely with `--worklog-dir` when operating there.

## Problem Statement

When the main checkout's `dev` is fast-forwarded mid-test-run by a sibling
`implement.py finish`, a suite produces failures that exist in **no single
commit** (tests from X, source from Y). The test-failure triage logic can mint
phantom `test-failure` work items from such mixed-tree output, creating noise
and false work for producers (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a producer, I want the triage logic to detect and suppress known phantom
patterns (mixed-tree verdicts from a moving checkout) so they no longer
auto-mint critical `test-failure` work items, while genuine failures still
triage normally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No phantom test-failure items:** after the mitigation, the race no longer
   generates additional phantom test-failure work items without manual triage;
   existing test-failure triage logic detects and suppresses known phantom
   patterns.
2. The test-failure triage helper detects known phantom signatures — a
   `state_changed_during_run` / mid-run fast-forward flag, or output recorded
   while the executing checkout was not a stable, pinned tree — and suppresses
   auto-creation of a `test-failure` work item, recording the suppression
   reason instead.
3. A suppressed phantom is still reported in the run's output/report with an
   explicit notice (`state_changed_during_run` notice code or equivalent),
   so the information is never silently lost — it is simply not minted as a
   critical item.
4. A genuine failure on a stable checkout still creates/updates a
   `test-failure` work item exactly as before (no behaviour change for real
   failures).

# Implement left-of-extensions tab placement for interactive dispatches

## Summary

Add an interactive-placement mode to the tab-creation path so operator-created tabs appear left of the Worklog/extensions tab; dispatcher tabs remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An interactive dispatch that creates a new tab (ID-carrying commands such as `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, prompt/`!!`/`!` commands carrying a work-item ID, and a new-pi-session dispatch from the selection list) places that tab immediately to the left of the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab in the invoking workspace.
- Automated dispatches (downtime dispatcher) place their tabs at the default right-side position exactly as today — no behaviour change.
- Tab repositioning is implemented via the herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` set to the extensions tab's index (or an equivalent herdr CLI/socket mechanism available at implement time); the tab is first created as today and then moved.
- Fail-open: when the Worklog/extensions tab cannot be resolved (no plugin pane, no tab labelled `Worklog`, multiple/ambiguous matches) or `tab.move` fails, the newly created tab stays at its default right-side position — the dispatch is never blocked, dropped, or placed in a wrong workspace.
- Reuse semantics are preserved: an existing item-ID tab is adopted without being moved (only freshly provisioned tabs are repositioned; a reused tab's position is the operator's own arrangement).
- At least one automated test (unit or integration) covers each of: left placement for an interactively created tab, default right placement for a dispatcher-created tab, and fail-open when the extensions tab or the move is unavailable.

## Implementation approach

1. Add a `moveTabInWorkspace` helper to `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` using the herdr socket API (`tab.move` with `insert_index`).
2. Add a `resolveExtensionsTab` helper to `dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` that finds the extensions tab and returns its index, failing open on ambiguity.
3. Add a `placement` flag/param to `createTabInWorkspace` and `DispatcherAnchorDeps.createTab` (default `right`, new option `left-of-extensions`).
4. In `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` / `getItemTabAnchor` interactive provisioning path: when a fresh tab is created (signalled by `onCreate`), move it left of the extensions tab using the new helpers.
5. Dispatcher path (`dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` / `downtime-worker.pane.ts`) remains untouched.
6. Add tests alongside each module.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — `createTabInWorkspace` and new `moveTabInWorkspace` helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `resolveExtensionsTab` helper; interactive provisioning path in `getItemTabAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — new `PlacementMode` type and `moveTab` dep.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` forwarding.
- Tests alongside each module.

## Constraints

- No herdr core changes in scope.
- Fail-open at every boundary.
- Dispatcher path unchanged.
- Reused tabs are never moved.

## Related work

- WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — "Implement: interactive item-tab placement" (completed)
- WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ — decomposed `dispatcher-anchor.ts`
